title.rendered: Self-Control: The Fruit of the Spirit | Day 9

excerpt.rendered: Ancient Greek athletes trained under enkrateia. Mastery within. The athlete’s discipline. Paul reached for that word to name the ninth and final fruit of the Spirit.

content.rendered:
The ancient Greek athletes preparing for the Olympic Games followed a ten-month training regimen so demanding it had its own word. Enkrateia. The self-mastery of the athlete. Paul reached for that word to name the ninth and final fruit of the Spirit.

The Gospel For Today | Thursday, October 2, 2026 | The Fruit of the Spirit, Day 9

Today’s Scripture

“But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, longsuffering, kindness, goodness, faithfulness, gentleness, self-control. Against such there is no law.”
Galatians 5:22-23 (NKJV)

Today’s Message

The ancient Greek athletes preparing for the Olympic Games at Elis followed a ten-month training regimen that was so demanding it had its own word. Enkrateia. It combined the Greek en (in, within) with kratos (power, mastery). Literally, mastery within. Self-mastery. The athlete’s discipline. For ten months before the games, every athlete lived under a strict code. Their diet was controlled. Their sleep was controlled. Their training hours were controlled. Their sexual activity was controlled. Everything the athlete did was subordinated to the single goal of arriving at Elis in peak form. Paul reached for that specific and powerful athletic word when he came to the ninth and final fruit of the Spirit in Galatians 5:23. Self-control. The mastery within, produced by the Spirit, that enables a believer to say no to what would derail them and yes to what advances them in Christ.

Paul was fond of athletic metaphors, and he used enkrateia repeatedly in his letters. In 1 Corinthians 9:25, writing to a church that lived within walking distance of the Isthmian Games, he says, “And everyone who competes for the prize is temperate in all things. Now they do it to obtain a perishable crown, but we for an imperishable crown.” The Greek word for “temperate” there is the verb form of enkrateia. Paul is telling the Corinthians that the same self-mastery the athletes practise for a wreath of dying leaves, believers are called to practise for an eternal reward. The difference is that the athletes work it up through willpower. The believer, according to Galatians 5, has it grown in them by the Holy Spirit.

The Passion Translation opens up the depth of what the Spirit produces: “But the fruit produced by the Holy Spirit within you is divine love in all its varied expressions: joy that overflows, peace that subdues, patience that endures, kindness in action, a life full of virtue, faith that prevails, gentleness of heart, and strength of spirit” (Galatians 5:22-23 TPT). Strength of spirit. The Amplified Bible Classic Edition adds: “But the fruit of the (Holy) Spirit [the work which His presence within accomplishes] is love, joy (gladness), peace, patience (an even temper, forbearance), kindness, goodness (benevolence), faithfulness, gentleness (meekness, humility), self-control (self-restraint, continence)” (Galatians 5:22-23 AMPC). Self-restraint. Continence. The Spirit-formed capacity to govern the appetites, to master the impulses, to say no to what the flesh would drag us toward and yes to what the Spirit is leading us into.

This is why the New Testament closes the list of the fruit of the Spirit with self-control. Every other fruit that comes before it depends on this one for its consistent expression in the believer’s life. A person may feel a rush of love in a moment and yet not have the self-control to keep loving when the moment passes. A person may feel a burst of joy and yet not have the self-control to protect the joy from the next distraction. Self-control is the fruit that guards every other fruit. It is the Spirit-produced strength to keep walking in what the Spirit has produced, even when the flesh would prefer a shortcut.

For Gospelbuzz readers today, this closes our nine-day walk through the fruit of the Spirit. Wherever you are reading this from, in Lagos or London or Manila or Nairobi or Sao Paulo, you are not called to manufacture self-control through gritted teeth and willpower. You are called to yield to the Spirit who is producing it in you. Feed on the Word. Return to the cross. Stay rooted in Christ. And let the Spirit grow, over the season of your walk with Him, the same strength of soul the ancient athletes trained for. Yours will not perish with the crown. Yours will echo into eternity.

Prayer

Father, I acknowledge that self-control is a fruit of Your Spirit in my life. Not manufactured through willpower. Grown in me by the Holy Spirit as I stay rooted in Christ. Today I yield to that work. I refuse to try to control myself through gritted teeth. I feed on Your Word. I return to the cross. I stay in the presence of the Spirit. And I trust Him to produce in me the mastery within that enables me to say no to what would derail me and yes to what You are leading me into. In Jesus’ name. Amen.

Declaration

Self-control is the fruit of the Spirit in my life today. The mastery within has been produced in me by the Holy Spirit as I stay rooted in Christ. I say no to what would derail me. I say yes to what the Spirit is leading me into.
